headline: High: shared writable workspaces and broad egress make Dify↔nullclaw pair prone to data leakage, prompt injection, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write uploaded knowledge base files and uses tools wired into agent/workflow apps; nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use browser/MCP, and has stdin/stdout plus webhooks. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from shared files or web channels. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are written into a shared workspace that nullclaw reads as instructions, injection becomes actionable.
IF nullclaw ingests browser/webhook content without provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Require human review before tool execution on imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read/write filesystem access, and both touch sensitive classes: Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, and secrets; nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs. If they share a workspace or datastore, either can expose the other's sensitive material to external services by default.
conditions: IF the two agents share any filesystem or datastore path, sensitive files can cross from one agent into the other's context.
IF either agent forwards file contents to model providers or web APIs, secrets in those files can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate OS users and directories.
Block outbound access for sensitive folders.
Redact secrets before any model/API call.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; nullclaw also modifies git state and uses MCP, while Dify runs server-side code tools in a sandbox container. If they target the same repo, workspace, or mutable resource, concurrent writes and state drift are likely without explicit locking. The profiles show overlapping write surfaces on both sides.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering or inconsistent outputs can occur.
IF nullclaw's git operations and Dify's file writes touch the same repo, state corruption becomes plausible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable git mutation in shared runs.
Snapshot before each agent acts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, and nullclaw has scheduler, delegate, webhook, and browser actions that can act on those outputs. If nullclaw treats Dify's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or repeated automation. This is a default-risk pathway because both profiles expose action-taking surfaces.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes Dify-generated text as a task plan, it may execute incorrect actions.
IF Dify-produced facts are routed into nullclaw's scheduler or webhook handlers without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require schema validation on exchanged messages.
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for Dify outputs.
Log and review all delegated actions.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge base content, while nullclaw touches audit logs, workspace files, and many secret-bearing classes. Their docs do not show aligned retention, residency, or subject-rights controls, so combining them can create mismatched handling of the same data class. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair's differing storage and logging surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, retention and deletion obligations may diverge.
IF one agent logs content that the other treats as ephemeral, compliance records can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Classify data before routing.
Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Align retention settings manually.
Review logging defaults in both systems.
requires-engineering: document a joint data-processing agreement.
